key_highlights: ASX shed $90b in a week amid rate-rise fears and oil surge, but edged higher on the day as Fed meeting looms
Iron ore crash confirmed with 'bloodletting' underway, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
10-year US Treasury yield hit 4.94%, heightening global rate concerns
Australian fuel prices set to rise 30c/litre on oil spike, squeezing consumer margins
ANZ.AX restructuring continues post-3,500 job cuts; private hospital operator to be broken up
Mining cap raises accelerate as Canaccord-led dash for cash signals sector stress
No spring bounce in Australian auction market; house price decline continues
Santos (STO.AX) preservation deal seen as national sacrifice for energy security

sectors.trend: Severely negative. Iron ore in confirmed crash with 'bloodletting' underway. Large-cap miners under pressure; small-caps (PolarX, Sunstone, Manuka) showing relative strength. Cap raises accelerating as miners scramble for liquidity.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression. Small-cap miners (ASX: small caps) offer speculative upside but cap-raise dilution risk is elevated. Avoid large-cap iron ore exposure short-term.

sectors.trend: Mixed. ANZ.AX restructuring post-3,500 cuts signals ongoing cost discipline but execution risk. 10-year US yield at 4.94% pressures global bank valuations. Rate-rise fears weigh on ASX banks.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX face NIM pressure if RBA holds or cuts. Monitor ANZ restructuring progress. Defensive quality in CBA.AX, WBC.AX preferred.

sectors.trend: Positive for producers, negative for consumers. Oil spike lifts Santos (STO.AX) and Woodside (WDS.AX). Fuel prices rising 30c/litre domestically. Santos preservation deal signals government energy-security priority.
sectors.implications: STO.AX, WDS.AX benefit from oil strength. Qantas (QAN.AX) and airlines face margin pressure. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) face input cost inflation.

sectors.trend: Structural shift. Major private hospital operator breakup via lender-backed consortium signals consolidation in ASX healthcare/health services.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX (defensive) remains a core holding. Hospital operator breakup may create M&A opportunities in health services. Monitor for spin-off or acquisition targets.

sectors.trend: Negative. No spring bounce in auction market; house prices falling. Fuel price rise and migration policy uncertainty dampen consumer confidence. Retail weakness (jewellery chain closing 53 stores).
sectors.implications: REITs (GPG.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and rate sensitivity. WES.AX, WOW.AX under pressure from fuel costs. Defensive consumer staples preferred.

sectors.trend: Globally positive. Nvidia's $10B Anthropic investment, AMD upside, Alibaba AI bet signal continued AI capex cycle. ASX small-caps (Neurizon, Iondrive) showing momentum.
sectors.implications: ASX tech exposure limited but small-cap AI/tech names (Neurizon, Iondrive) offer speculative upside. Global AI capex supports sentiment but valuations stretched.

key_themes: Iron ore crash and mining sector liquidity stress
Global rate fears: 10Y US yield at 4.94%, Fed meeting catalyst
Oil spike driving fuel inflation and consumer squeeze
Australian housing market in sustained correction
Migration policy uncertainty (One Nation, visa pauses) creating labour and demand risk
Energy security: Santos preservation as national priority
AI capex cycle continues globally but ASX exposure limited
ANZ restructuring and banking sector cost discipline

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX exposure; rotate into gold (NEM.AX, GOLD.AX) and energy

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Global rate shock / Fed hawkish surprise
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge with short-duration bonds; favour quality dividend payers (CBA.AX, WBC.AX, SGP.AX)
Overweight energy producers; underweight airlines (QAN.AX) and discretionary consumer
Reduce REIT exposure; monitor building sector (WBC.AX, CGW.AX) for credit stress
Monitor agricultural and services sector earnings; policy risk is binary
Avoid small-cap miners with imminent cap raises; favour cash-flow-positive large caps

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight energy producers on oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Oil surge supports STO.AX, WDS.AX earnings; Santos preservation deal adds policy tailwind

opportunities.recommendation: Rotate into gold and defensive materials
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore crash makes gold (NEM.AX, GOLD.AX) and copper (BHP.AX copper segment) relatively attractive
Neurizon, Iondrive showing momentum; global AI capex cycle (Nvidia, AMD) supports sentiment

opportunities.recommendation: Quality dividend banks as rate hedge
opportunities.rationale: CBA.AX, WBC.AX offer 6%+ yields; ANZ restructuring may create relative value

defensive_moves.rationale: Confirmed crash with bloodletting; cap-raise dilution risk in small caps
No auction bounce, falling prices, rate sensitivity; credit risk building
10Y US yield at 4.94%, Fed meeting risk; AUD under pressure from commodity weakness
30c fuel rise, one flight cancelled every 3 days, margin compression

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish-to-neutral. ASX faces headwinds from iron ore crash, oil-driven fuel inflation, and Fed meeting uncertainty. $90b weekly loss signals risk-off. Expect volatility around Fed decision. Key support at prior lows; any hawkish Fed surprise could trigger further selling.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Iron ore crash may be cyclical; energy security policy supports STO.AX, WDS.AX. AI capex cycle and ANZ restructuring offer medium-term value. Housing correction may stabilise by H2 2026. RBA likely to cut if growth slows, supporting equities.

Australian fuel price pass-through to CPI
Migration policy finalisation (One Nation vs Labor)
watch_list: Brent crude and Australian domestic fuel prices
Housing auction clearance rates and price indices
China trade policy and Arctic shipping route developments
